title: Inside the Venture Studio Model: Why We Build This Way
excerpt: Accelerators mentor, funds finance, agencies execute. A venture studio does something different: it builds companies as its core product. Here's how the model works — and when it wins.
content:
When we tell people Alttene is a venture studio, we usually get one of two reactions: a polite nod, or the honest question — what is that, actually? Fair. The term gets used loosely. So here's the model as we practice it.

The four ways to make startups

Most startup-adjacent institutions fit one of four shapes:

  • Accelerators take in existing teams, sharpen them for a few months, and connect them to capital.

  • Venture funds pick founders and write cheques, betting on other people's execution.

  • Agencies execute someone else's vision for a fee, then hand over the keys.

  • Venture studios generate ideas in-house, build them with an in-house team, and spin out the ones that find traction.

The studio is the only shape where the institution itself is the founder. That changes everything about incentives: we don't advise from the sidelines and we don't bill by the hour. If the product doesn't work, we eat that outcome.

Why the model compounds

A studio's real asset isn't any single company — it's the repeatable machinery: shared design systems, a bench of playbooks for launch and growth, distribution relationships, and the scar tissue from every previous build. Each venture starts further from zero than the last. The failures are cheaper, the wins arrive faster, and the learning never walks out the door the way it does when an agency project ends.

The honest trade-offs

The model isn't magic. Focus is the tax: every additional build competes for the same senior attention, which is why we cap ourselves at one flagship product at a time. Capital efficiency is the discipline: studios that spray ten half-built apps a year mostly produce ten funerals. Our bar is simple — we don't start something new until the current thing can survive a quarter without us hovering.

Where Alttene fits

Koffeechat is the flagship build. Alto Partners lets us run our playbooks inside other people's companies, which keeps the machinery sharp and honest. Fisayo.org makes sure the compounding isn't only financial. One studio, three fronts, one operating system.

If you're weighing whether to join a startup, back one, or build inside a studio — the short version is this: pick the structure whose incentives you'd want on your worst day. Ours are simple. We only win when the thing we built works.
